acute_alarm.userFacingLabel: Your brain's alarm system is activated right now
acute_alarm.description: Phasic/immediate threat response with amygdala-driven arousal and suppressed prefrontal regulation
safetyConstraints: Do not say 'amygdala hijacking'
Frame as current state not trait
Use 'right now' not 'you tend to'
acute_alarm.clinicalNotes: BNST involvement scales with sustained/uncertain threat. LC-NE amplifies arousal. Hippocampus suppression = contextual safety signaling less effective.

chronic_vigilance.userFacingLabel: Your attention is locked onto what could go wrong
chronic_vigilance.description: Sustained/anticipatory threat processing with BNST as primary driver; radar stuck on mode
safetyConstraints: Superior colliculus REJECTED as core node - sparse human fMRI evidence
chronic_vigilance.clinicalNotes: BNST specialized for defensive distance. Treatment levers: attentional retraining and safety-signal conditioning vs autonomic downshift for acute alarm.

conservation_freeze.userFacingLabel: Your system is conserving energy right now
conservation_freeze.description: PAG-centered shutdown/freeze; global dampening with no single dominant network
safetyConstraints: CRITICAL: Traditional calming tools may worsen state
Do NOT recommend deep breathing or meditation
Favor gentle up-regulation: cold water, proprioceptive input, micro-movements
Pulling out too quickly can trigger rebound panic
conservation_freeze.clinicalNotes: Model PAG as coordinator NOT 'Dorsal Vagal Complex'. Use neutral ANS terminology. Thalamic suppression reduces sensory bandwidth contributing to dissociative experiences.

dissociation_overmodulation.userFacingLabel: Your mind is protecting you by disconnecting
dissociation_overmodulation.description: PFC OVER-active suppressing limbic response; distinct from global dampening of conservation_freeze
dissociation_overmodulation.evidenceGrade: Strong within PTSD-dissociative subtype; Moderate for broader DPDR
safetyConstraints: Dissociation + suicidal ideation = escalation pathway
Do NOT suggest heavy interoceptive exposure without titration
Somatic Experiencing and gentle proprioceptive input are safer entry points
dissociation_overmodulation.clinicalNotes: Control tower actively silencing alarms. Needs interoceptive reconnection - slowly re-establishing contact with suppressed body signals. Amygdala SUPPRESSION is defining feature.

emotional_flooding.userFacingLabel: Your feelings are hitting all at once
emotional_flooding.description: PFC essentially offline; salience network overloaded; cognitive tools will fail in this state
safetyConstraints: Screen for self-harm risk when 'out of control' reported
Emergency state - present tools immediately with minimal cognitive demand
No browsing, 1-2 options max
emotional_flooding.clinicalNotes: OFC suppression is key differentiator - cannot reason about emotion. MUST recommend bottom-up autonomic tools: cold water, paced breathing, PMR. dlPAG involvement (active defense) included with moderate evidence.

grief_yearning.userFacingLabel: Your attachment system is reaching for who is gone
grief_yearning.description: NAc/ventral striatum yearning/craving, PCC autobiographical memory, amygdala distress
safetyConstraints: Never use 'moving on' language
Focus on integrated memory and meaning-making
Do not pathologize normal grief trajectories
grief_yearning.clinicalNotes: NAc findings specific to PROLONGED/COMPLICATED grief. Do not generalize to all grief.

reactive_aggression.userFacingLabel: Your protection system is translating stress into anger
reactive_aggression.description: Amygdala-hypothalamus-PAG attack circuit with suppressed regulatory PFC nodes
safetyConstraints: Proactive/instrumental aggression REJECTED for all releases
Only reactive aggression modeled
Requires careful tool sequencing to avoid escalation
reactive_aggression.clinicalNotes: Higher safety complexity. Tools must discharge sympathetic energy safely before cognitive tools. Affect labeling re-engages vlPFC. High association with hostile attribution bias.

reward_drive_low.userFacingLabel: Your motivation system is idling right now
reward_drive_low.description: Ventral striatal blunting with reduced dopamine signaling; positive valence system under-engaged
reward_drive_low.evidenceGrade: Strong for ventral striatal blunting; Moderate for inflammation mechanism
safetyConstraints: Screen for MDE if anhedonia pervasive across multiple check-ins
Consider fatigue/inflammation screening if persistent
Do NOT imply 'not trying hard enough'
reward_drive_low.clinicalNotes: Frame as 'reward system under-engaged' not single-cause. Inflammation→dopamine suppression is emerging evidence only - NOT inferable from self-report. High-effort goal setting may backfire. Recommend low-friction behavioral activation with small immediate sensory rewards.

rumination_loop.userFacingLabel: Your mind is stuck on replay
rumination_loop.description: DMN hyperactivity with sgACC coupling; self-referential processing infused with negative valence
rumination_loop.evidenceGrade: Strong for depressive rumination; Moderate for anxious worry
safetyConstraints: If ruminative content involves suicidal ideation trigger crisis pathways
Do not use 'brain is broken' framing
rumination_loop.clinicalNotes: DMN and sgPFC create caustic compound when functionally linked. dlPFC suppression NOT universal - may be active but failing in anxious worry. Break the link via task-positive activities requiring external focus. Mindfulness can backfire by increasing internal focus.

social_threat_shame.userFacingLabel: Your brain is treating social evaluation like danger
social_threat_shame.description: Self-evaluation-forward rather than amygdala-forward; intense Theory-of-Mind engagement modeling negative gaze of others
safetyConstraints: Emphasize self-compassion and common humanity
Avoid tools that increase self-focus (journaling may amplify shame)
Do not suggest hopelessness/worthlessness as co-occurring without extreme care
social_threat_shame.clinicalNotes: Shame activates behavioral inhibition (hide/freeze). Guilt activates TPJ/reparative action. Social rejection activates dACC/insula pain. vmPFC suppression is state-dependent. Can trigger reactive aggression to regain social status.

cbt_exposure.name: Exposure
cbt_exposure.description: Gradually facing feared situations to reduce anxiety through extinction learning

dbt_alternate_rebellion.name: Alternate Rebellion
dbt_alternate_rebellion.description: Finding non-destructive ways to rebel when feeling controlled or wanting to act against expectations; channel rebellious urges into harmless or even positive actions
dbt_alternate_rebellion.whenToUse: When feeling controlled, wanting to defy expectations, or having urges to do something destructive just to rebel

dbt_dear_man.name: DEAR MAN
dbt_dear_man.description: Describe, Express, Assert, Reinforce, Mindful, Appear confident, Negotiate

dbt_find_the_feeling.name: Find the Feeling
dbt_find_the_feeling.description: Identify and name an emotion without introspective rating: match it to a shape or a sound, then accept or refuse an offered word
dbt_find_the_feeling.whenToUse: When you can tell something's there but not what it is
dbt_find_the_feeling.dbtBasis: Emotion Regulation: observing, describing and naming emotions (with Mindfulness Describe), without numeric rating

dbt_opposite_action.name: Opposite Action
dbt_opposite_action.description: Acting opposite to emotion urge when emotion doesn't fit facts or isn't effective

dbt_problem_solving.name: Problem Solving
dbt_problem_solving.description: Changing the situation when emotion fits the facts

dbt_recovering_from_invalidation.name: Recovering from Invalidation
dbt_recovering_from_invalidation.description: Body-first sequence after someone dismisses, mocks, excludes or pulls away: settle, name it, self-validate, name the need, then ask (DEAR MAN), let it land, or act opposite
dbt_recovering_from_invalidation.whenToUse: When someone brushed you off, mocked you, left you out, or pulled away
dbt_recovering_from_invalidation.dbtBasis: Walking the Middle Path (validation, recovering from invalidation) with STOP, TIPP, Opposite Action and Radical Acceptance; asking hands off to DEAR MAN

dbt_stop.name: STOP
dbt_stop.description: Stop, Take a step back, Observe, Proceed mindfully

dbt_tipp.name: TIPP
dbt_tipp.description: Temperature, Intense exercise, Paced breathing, Paired muscle relaxation

se_orienting.name: Orienting
se_orienting.description: Natural scanning of environment that was interrupted during trauma

urge_surfing.name: Urge Surfing
urge_surfing.description: Watching an urge rise, peak and fall without acting on it

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your alarm system activated and your mind pulled away at the same time — that's a protective response
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Grounding and safety-signal conditioning first (alarm protocol — orient to present safety). Once alarm subsides, dissociation often resolves spontaneously since it was protective. If dissociation persists after alarm resolves, then gentle sensory reconnection. Do NOT process the triggering event while either pattern is active.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your system has been on guard for a long time and is running out of fuel
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Gentle proprioceptive up-regulation first (restore baseline body awareness and minimal sense of agency). The system is resource-depleted — demanding cognitive or regulatory effort will fail. Once body is minimally mobilized, then safety-signal conditioning and autonomic settling (vigilance protocol). Also: address sleep and basic needs as top priority.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your alarm system is running in the background, and it's draining your ability to enjoy things
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Autonomic down-regulation + safety-signal conditioning first (vigilance protocol) to reduce threat bias that is actively suppressing reward system. Once body settles, micro-behavioral-activation (reward protocol). Behavioral activation fails while threat-scanning is active — person cannot engage with rewarding activities while on guard.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your alarm system is scanning for threats, and your mind is building worst-case scenarios
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Autonomic down-regulation first (grounding, paced breathing, safety-signal conditioning) to reduce tonic sympathetic activation. This lowers SN threat bias and starves the worry loop. Then attention redirection (rumination protocol). Note: calming tools ARE appropriate here — vigilance is high-arousal, unlike freeze.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your system has gone very still, and your connection to your body is faint right now
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Proprioceptive grounding first (micro-movements, warmth, bilateral input) to restore bottom-up sensory signals through thalamus. Only then titrated interoceptive reconnection (dissociation protocol). Asking someone to 'notice body sensations' during freeze fails because signals aren't getting through.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your mind is looping, but it feels like you're watching it from a distance
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Gentle sensory reconnection first (dissociation protocol) to re-establish body-brain signal path. This may briefly intensify emotional experience of ruminative content — that is expected and necessary. Once reconnected, external-focus tasks (rumination protocol) become effective. Do NOT start with attention redirection — person is already 'distant' from experience.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your body is activated, but your mind has pulled away to protect you
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Autonomic down-regulation first (cold water, paced breathing, bilateral stimulation — bottom-up only, NO cognitive tools). Once body activation subsides, then gentle sensory reconnection (dissociation protocol). Do NOT start with interoceptive reconnection — opening the gate to the body while it's flooded risks re-flooding.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your motivation system is idling, and your mind is trying to figure out why
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Micro-behavioral-activation first (tiniest possible rewarding action to generate dopamine signal), then attention redirection if rumination persists. Rumination diminishes when something rewarding is available. Do NOT start with external-focus tasks — nothing is salient enough to redirect to.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: Your mind is stuck on replay, and your body has gone still to protect you
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Proprioceptive up-regulation first (restore motor system and baseline CEN capacity), then external-focus attention tasks (rumination protocol). CEN engagement requires arousal that freeze suppresses.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: The weight of being seen has made your whole system go still
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Gentle proprioceptive up-regulation first (restore minimal body engagement). Once minimally mobilized, self-compassion touch + outward sensory contact (social threat protocol). Do NOT start with self-focused tools (amplifies shame) or social engagement demands (behavioral inhibition system is blocking this). Warmth is especially helpful — warm beverage, blanket — signals safety without social demand.

coOccurrence.combinedUserFacingLabel: You're replaying a social moment, and the shame is keeping the loop going
coOccurrence.sequencingNote: Outward-directed sensory contact + self-compassion touch first (social threat protocol). This breaks self-focused attention that feeds both shame-body and ruminative loop. Once shame activation decreases, ruminative content loses emotional charge. Then external-focus tasks if loop persists.
